title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Elena Chen
summary: Canonical set of architecture and engineering standards for APIs, code, infrastructure, model serving, observability, and performance at Redwood Inference, plus linked ADR summaries and ownership.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards covering API design, coding guidelines, infrastructure IaC patterns, model-serving best practices, observability requirements, performance SLOs, and a short index of recent Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). It is intended for engineers designing new services, shipping model endpoints, and writing infra or platform-level changes.

Scope
- API standards (REST/JSON, versioning, error handling, pagination, auth)
- Coding standards and PR/branch hygiene
- Infra and IaC standards (Terraform modules, cloud accounts, networking)
- Model-serving standards (model variants, quantization, fallback policies, KV cache)
- Observability standards (metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerts)
- Performance standards (latency SLOs, throughput benchmarking, cost controls)
- ADR index and decision guidance

1) API Standards
Purpose: Provide stable, discoverable, and debuggable HTTP APIs for clients and internal services.

Key rules:
- API contract: JSON over HTTPS, prefer application/json; for streaming completions use text/event-stream with chunked transfer.
- Versioning: Use URI versioning for breaking changes: /v1/, /v2/. For non-breaking additions, extend the response schema and mark fields "nullable" where appropriate.
- Idempotency: Require an X-Request-Id header where client retries are expected. For mutating endpoints, support idempotency-key header for safe retries.
- Authentication: All endpoints must validate tokens issued by our control plane: Authorization: Bearer <token>. Private deployments may use mutual TLS; document in deployment guide.
- Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination. Response example: { "items": [...], "next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwfQ==" }
- Errors: Standardize errors to structure { "code": "string", "message": "human readable", "details": {...} } and use HTTP codes per semantics (400/401/403/404/409/429/500). Include an error_id header for server-side correlation (X-Error-Id).
- Rate limiting: Return 429 with Retry-After header. Include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset for public endpoints.

API design checklist (for owners):
1. Define input/output JSON schema in OpenAPI (required).
2. Add example requests/responses.
3. Document auth scopes and rate-limit class.
4. Add integration tests that validate schema and error paths.
5. Add a contract test that runs in CI against the staging API.

Example OpenAPI snippet (yaml):
---
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Generate text
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerationRequest'
---

2) Coding Standards and PR Process
Goals: Consistent, reviewable, and high-quality code across services.

Rules:
- Language conventions: Follow the community styleguide for each language (PEP8 for Python, gofmt for Go, rustfmt for Rust, Google style for Typescript).
- Linting: All repo-level linters must pass in CI. Examples: eslint for js/ts, flake8 + black for python, golangci-lint for Go.
- Formatting: Enforce auto-formatters on pre-commit hooks.
- Tests: Minimum coverage: critical modules must have unit tests exercising edge cases. PRs must include unit tests for new logic and regression tests for fixed bugs.
- Types: Prefer static types where supported (TypeScript, Go, Rust); add typedefs for public library surfaces.
- Secrets: No secrets in code. Use vault/KMS integrations and environment variables injected by deployment pipelines.
- PR process:
  1. Small, focused PRs (ideally < 500 LOC).
  2. Set reviewers from owning team and at least one cross-team reviewer for infra-impacting changes.
  3. Link the PR to the JIRA ticket and relevant ADR if applicable.
  4. Ensure CI (unit, integration, contract, security checks) is green before merge.
  5. Use feature flags for user-facing or risky changes; follow the rollout checklist below.

Branch and release conventions:
- Branches: feature/<short-desc>, fix/<issue-number>-<short>, hotfix/<short>.
- Releases: Use semver for libraries; services use a rolling deployment process with canary releases.

3) Infra and IaC Standards
Goal: Stable, reproducible infrastructure with minimal blast radius and clear ownership.

- Terraform modules: Publish shared modules in infra-modules repo. Modules must be documented and pinned by major version.
- State backend: Use remote state in a central S3 bucket with DynamoDB locking. States are per-environment (prod, staging, dev).
- Cloud accounts/networking:
  - Each customer Private deployment gets a dedicated VPC/Account when required by compliance.
  - Internal services use dedicated subnets per tier (ingress, inference, internal services).
  - Use standardized tag keys: Owner, Environment, Project, CostCenter.
- Secrets management: Use KMS for envelope encryption; secrets stored in Vault with automatic rotation policies.
- CI/CD: Pipeline must run terraform plan and require manual approval for prod apply. Non-prod can be auto-applied after CI checks.
- Canary and rollback: Use blue/green or canary with automated health checks (see rollout procedure).

IaC checklist:
1. Module author documents variables, outputs, and example usage.
2. Add unit-style tests (terratest) and policy-as-code (OPA) checks.
3. Validate plan drift monthly for prod state.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Purpose: Ensure models are served reliably with predictable latency, correct fallbacks, and controlled cost.

- Model packaging: All production models must include a manifest.json containing: model_id, version, architecture, quantization_profile, tokenizer_version, compatible_runtime_tags.
- Quantization: Quantization profiles are approved by Applied ML; recommended defaults: FP16 for high-accuracy variants, 8-bit quantized variants for cost-sensitive low-latency paths. Each profile must include accuracy regression tests (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine).
- Variant strategy: Provide at least two variants per major model: quality variant (higher precision) and cost variant (quantized). Use routing policy to prefer quality variant with automatic fallback to cost variant under capacity pressure.
- KV cache and prefix caching: Cache keys must be eviction-safe; identify prefixes in request metadata. Default TTLs: 5min for session-level caches, 24h for common prompt fragments.
- Runtime compatibility: Tag models with runtime features (e.g., kv-cache-v2, fused-attn). The runtime will only accept models with matching tags.
- Rollout for model updates:
  1. Upload model to staging storage and run offline evals against benchmark prompt sets.
  2. Deploy to staging cluster and run synthetic load tests (target p95 latency under 2x prod SLO).
  3. Canary deploy to 5% of production traffic for 24h with active monitoring of QPS, latency, and quality metrics.
  4. Gradually increase to 20% then 50% before full rollout; abort on quality regression or >5% increase in p95 latency.

Model serving checklist for owners:
- Include manifest.json, eval reports, canary config, and rollback tag.

5) Observability Standards
Goals: Ensure incidents are detectable, triage is fast, and regressions are visible.

- Metrics:
  - Every service must emit: requests_total, requests_failed_total (by code/class), request_latency_seconds_bucket (histogram), and resource metrics (cpu, gpu_util, mem).
  - For model endpoints add per-model metrics: tokens_generated_total, tokens_cached_total, avg_kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Traces: Instrument critical request paths with distributed traces (OpenTelemetry). Capture spans for auth, routing, runtime execution, and external calls (S3, KMS).
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, shard, model_id, request_id, error_id, message. Logs should avoid PII and sensitive payloads.
- Dashboards: Standard dashboards required:
  - Service health: error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput.
  - Model health: per-model latency, quality trends (eval diffs), cache hit rates.
  - Infrastructure: GPU utilization, queue depths, pod restart rates.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - P95 latency > 2x SLO for 5m -> page oncall SRE.
  - Error rate > 1% of requests for 5m -> warn on-call, escalate if >5% for 10m.
  - GPU mem pressure > 90% for 10m -> pager.

- Runbook linkage: Every alert must reference a runbook with triage steps, mitigation, and rollback. Keep runbooks in confluence under eng-sre/runbooks.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarks
SLOs (service-level):
- Hosted API text generation endpoints:
  - Latency: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 220ms (short prompts), p95 < 1s (longer prompts up to 1024 tokens)
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly for hosted API (internal metric for Dedicated/Private SLAs can vary)
  - Cost guardrail: tokens_generated_cost_perk <= target defined per model profile (tracked in billing telemetry)

Benchmarking practices:
- Use the benchmarking-and-perf-suite repo to run throughput/latency tests against target hardware configurations.
- Synthetic load should include realistic prompt distributions (from analytics) and cold/hot cache profiles.
- Document kernel selection and quantization impacts on perf runs.

Performance regression criteria:
- A regression is any change that causes >10% increase in p95 latency or >5% increase in cost per token for the same quality. Such changes must be tied to an ADR or rollback.

7) ADR Index (short summaries)
This section lists recent Architecture Decision Records relevant to the above standards. Each ADR in full exists in the ADRs folder and is linked below.
- ADR-2025-11: runtime-kernel-selection
  - Decision: Use hybrid kernel selection that considers model architecture, sequence length distribution, and hardware.
  - Rationale: Empirically reduces p95 latency by 15% for long-context models.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime
- ADR-2026-02: default-quantization-profiles
  - Decision: Adopt three standard quantization profiles (fp16-quality, int8-cost, int4-experimental) with evaluation gates.
  - Rationale: Balance between quality and cost for most workloads.
  - Owner: applied-ml-and-evals
- ADR-2026-04: api-versioning-and-contract-testing
  - Decision: URI versioning + mandatory OpenAPI contract tests in CI.
  - Rationale: Simplify client routing and catch contract drift early.
  - Owner: eng-developer-experience

8) Rollout and Canary Procedure (summary)
Use this standardized canary flow for service and model updates:
1. Create canary config in deployment manifest (percentage, duration, success criteria).
2. Deploy canary to staging-like subset with synthetic traffic.
3. Deploy to production canary (5%) and monitor for at least 1 full business cycle (24h).
4. Auto-promote if no alerts and success criteria met; otherwise, abort and roll back.

Checklist before canary:
- All tests green in CI (unit, integration, contract, security scan)
- Metrics and tracing instrumented for new paths
- Runbook updated if new failure modes introduced

9) Ownership and Onboarding
- Ownership: Each service and infra module must declare an owning team in the service manifest (owner_team) and a primary pager on the SRE roster.
- Onboarding: New teams must complete a 1-hour standards review with eng-standards and a short checklist demonstrating CI, linting, monitoring, and ADR alignment.

10) How to propose a standards change (ADRs)
1. Draft an ADR using the template in /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-template (title, context, decision, consequences, alternatives, tests).
2. Open the ADR PR in the ADR repo and assign reviewers from affected teams.
3. After approval, link the ADR to relevant docs and update this standards page if needed.

Appendix: Example manifest.json for models
{
  "model_id": "redwood-tex-1",
  "version": "2026-05-01",
  "architecture": "decoder-only",
  "quantization_profile": "int8-cost",
  "tokenizer_version": "v3",
  "compatible_runtime_tags": ["kv-cache-v2", "fused-attn"]
}

Appendix: Example alert rule (Prometheus-style)
- alert: ServiceHighP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 2 * service_slo_p95
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "{{ $labels.service }} p95 latency is high"

Contact and maintenance
- Standards owner: eng-standards (eng-platform)
- Maintained by: Elena Chen (document owner), reviewed quarterly or when major infra/runtime changes occur.
- Questions: ping #eng-standards on Slack or open an issue in the internal docs repo.

This document is normative. Follow the checklists and link ADRs when deviating from standards.
